To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the illumination of accreting disks by an overlying source leads to the formation of several thermally stable layers in the illuminated gas.

the ionization balance in accretion discs is strongly affected by the thermal instability, and that the resulting temperature profiles are characterized by several well-defined thermally stable layers, with the temperature in each layer being determined by the local ionization state.
the thermal ionization instability in accretion discs prevents the gas from reaching the temperatures at which the ionization instability becomes important.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the illumination of accreting gas by an overlying source.
the illumination of accreting matter around compact objects by an external source of X-rays.
the study of the X-ray reflection from an ionized gas in the presence of a central X-ray source.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence of a strong ionizing radiation field, such as that produced by an accreting compact object, has a profound influence on the structure of the gas in the disk.

the X-ray reflection from the inner regions of the accretion disk around a compact object, as it is observed in the X-ray spectrum of the Galactic X-ray binary Cygnus X-1 and of the supermassive black hole at the center of the galaxy MCG-6-30-15, is consistent with an accretion disk with an outer radius at 2000 R _{g}, and a standard Shakura & Sunyaev viscosity parameter α = 0.
X-ray reflection from accretion disks around compact objects is a very complex phenomenon, which is still far from being fully understood.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the thermal ionization instability is a fundamental property of the gas in the vicinity of accretion flows and it has important implications for the interpretation of the X-ray emission from the innermost regions of the disks.
the thermal instability in accretion disk atmospheres is not only present, but also has a strong impact on the ionization balance.

we have demonstrated that the thermal instability in the illuminated gas is a robust feature and that its presence has important implications for the interpretation of the observed reflection spectra of X-ray sources.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a self-consistent treatment of the density profile is essential to obtain a correct understanding of the physics of the X-ray reflection process.
a detailed study of the thermal instability in the vicinity of a compact object requires the self-consistent determination of the gas density and the ionization balance.
the temperature of the gas in the vicinity of a compact source is determined by the thermal instability, and not by the ionization balance as is usually assumed in the literature.
